subject: Meteorology
title: Cloud Base and Top
description: A 60-second lesson on Cloud Base and Top.

hook.text: Every cloud has a flat bottom and a varied top—the base is where condensation starts, the top is where it stops.

buildup.text: Cloud base forms at the lifting condensation level—the height where rising air cools to its dew point.

discovery.text: Cloud tops are set by stability—in stable air, clouds flatten out; in unstable air, they tower upward.

twist.text: Thunderstorm tops can reach 15 km or higher—punching into the stratosphere and spreading into anvil shapes.

climax.text: Satellite imagery measures cloud-top temperature—colder tops mean taller, more powerful storms.

punchline.text: Flat base, variable top—clouds are built from below.
